blocking_findings.trigger: Change inline constexpr/enum values in a header consumed by a function whose definition bytes, definition range, ODRHash, and profile_id stay identical.
blocking_findings.key_result: case23ctx old index 9dc8ea33-055e-4f9c-962e-1758c5378889 -> new b1fbd1fe-55c9-492c-a75e-3563e7e8611c; same profile be097d7d...; leaf ODR 2280648299 both sides; root ODR 4026570732 both sides; definition bytes/ranges identical; unit_files includes settings.hpp both sides; diff-symbols returned_count=0, diff-calls returned_count=0, diff-files one file_text_changed for settings.hpp; behavior old leaf=4 root=5, new leaf=18 root=19. Codex probe independently inspected: old d78b1f35..., new f5c94406..., same empty symbols/calls and only value.hpp file_text_changed. d4 macro case fires but has no changed_inputs.
blocking_findings.impact: A real behavior-affecting header/read-set edit is reported as no function change in CLI/UI Diff; even the macro case lacks exact changed inputs, so the input/config cause is not stated. This violates the required M2-A Diff contract.
blocking_findings.minimal_fix: In diff.py _side load unit_files and files.sha256; for matched symbols with unchanged definition bytes compare hashes of read-set files for the symbol's observer units, excluding the symbol's own definition_file to preserve pure line-move behavior; emit definition_context_changed with changed_inputs [{path,before_sha256,after_sha256}]; keep ODRHash as an additional hint; when profile_id differs attach profile before/after in changed_inputs. No new analyzer architecture or M2-B required.
regression: New header constexpr/enum fixture: exactly one definition_context_changed for the consumer with changed_inputs containing the header's before/after SHA-256; no synthetic symbol/call deltas.
case05 macro header: context event remains and gains changed_inputs (header hash and/or profile pair).
Pure line-only move / blank lines outside range: only location_changed, site_location_changed, or ambiguous_correspondence; no definition_context_changed.
Shared header consumed by a and b but not c: context events only for actual observers; unrelated .cpp edit does not fire for other TUs.
-D/profile change: context event with profile before/after; configuration_changed coherent.
Document the same-file external constexpr residual of the minimal fix; do not claim it is covered.

blocking_findings.title: Source retrieval silently replaces non-UTF-8 indexed bytes with U+FFFD, so served bytes and SHA-256 do not match the indexed file
contract: acceptance.md:23 (case15): both sides serve original indexed byte slices and hashes
architecture.md:153: source response bounded saved buffer
blocking_findings.trigger: Index a C++ source containing a non-UTF-8 byte such as 0xFF, then query source via public CLI and HTTP.
blocking_findings.key_result: Indexed bad.cpp is 61 bytes, SHA-256 15f2e9e051325146407c36895472c96f0f54fc5e40ce825abbfccc89cb920029, containing 0xFF. CLI and HTTP source responses return U+FFFD replacement text; re-encoded served content is 63 bytes, SHA-256 99d4aec9575fe0a2de53b07dc036bc20553c5640b74ef0409f3be578459c2bb3. The response does not signal an error and has no sha256 field.
blocking_findings.impact: Users/clients cannot trust served source bytes or verify them against the immutable index; this violates the byte-slice/hash part of case15 for non-UTF-8 source.
blocking_findings.minimal_fix: Never use errors='replace'. Prefer a byte-safe representation (content_base64 plus content_encoding) for non-UTF-8 files; or fail closed with source_not_utf8. In either case expose the indexed SHA-256/range SHA-256 and ensure served bytes hash to it. Do not silently substitute.
regression: Index a file containing 0xFF; assert either explicit source_not_utf8 with no fake content, or base64 round-trip SHA equals the indexed file SHA-256.
Assert whole-file and range hashes match files.sha256 / definition_range.
Valid UTF-8 (Chinese/emoji/combining/CRLF) continues to round-trip exactly.

non_blocking_findings.title: source and source-diff responses lack a hash envelope
non_blocking_findings.key_result: Source payload keys are content,end_line,index_id,path,start_line; source-diff keys are comparison_id,left,right,left_index_id,right_index_id,unified_diff,windowed; nested content has no sha256. Diff-files and diff-symbols do carry hashes. Valid case15 content SHAs are d3b20c19... (157 bytes) and 85eb8716... (161 bytes).
non_blocking_findings.impact: A source response cannot be verified directly; combined with P2, byte substitution is invisible.
non_blocking_findings.minimal_fix: Add whole-file sha256 and range_sha256/buffer_sha256 to source and source-diff envelopes using existing files.sha256 and definition_range data; keep budgets; show/verify in CLI/UI.

limitations: P2/P3 interpretation is strict: case15's specified valid Unicode/emoji/combining/CRLF fixtures pass, but the contract text says original indexed byte slices and hashes without limiting to UTF-8; a real 0xFF source byte is silently replaced. If the product instead explicitly restricts sources to UTF-8, it must reject non-UTF-8 at the boundary rather than replace bytes, and the contract/error protocol must say so.

The proposed P1 minimal fix uses TU-level positive unit_files read-sets, not a complete include-resolution dependency model; it can conservatively fire for unused header changes in the same TU. This is input-context, not exact runtime causality.

Excluding a symbol's own definition_file to preserve pure line moves leaves a documented residual: an external constexpr in the same .cpp can still be missed. A per-definition read-set would be needed for that residual, but is not required for the reported header read-set case and would be a larger change.
ODRHash is nonauthoritative and cannot be used to prove no definition-context change; this is the root of P1.

The formal suite passes 132 backend tests and VERIFY_EXIT=0, but its macro tests (backend/tests/test_workspace.py:87 and frontend/e2e-m2/workspace.spec.ts:52) change ODR, so they do not cover the constexpr/enum ODR-invariant case and do not make case05 pass.

The Codex probe was inspected and its SHAs/argv/exit/JSON/unit_files verified, but its commands were not rerun one by one; the same class was independently reproduced with the different case23ctx fixture.

Candidate has no .git directory; Git modes were verified from executable permission bits according to the manifest rule, while the original source repository HEAD/branch were checked separately read-only.

Nine backend/codeweave/__pycache__/*.pyc files were created in the candidate directory by audit imports at 20:15:38. They are not in the manifest and were not deleted because deletion would alter the candidate; the 84 manifest files remain byte/mode identical.

The case16 own Git sentinel mtime was changed at 21:11:25 by the auditor's own `git -C ... status --porcelain` control command after the product trace at 20:13:55; product execve trace shows no hook/filter/sh execution. This is disclosed rather than claiming the sentinel was untouched.

No full implicit-call analysis, PCH/modules, whole-program virtual dispatch, M2-B, arbitrary historical builds, private projects, RMC/F11/reference, credentials, or network upload were attempted; they remain outside this audit.
No old ACCEPT is inherited. Round-2/3/4 interrupted records remain as history; this report is based only on the current round's evidence.

The parent agent's port 8000 demo server was not touched; audit HTTP servers on 18091/18097 were stopped after use. Case20 conclusions rely on saved real HTTP responses and Chromium logs, not on currently running services.
